title: Derived diagonal forces cotangent vanishing
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. If the canonical multiplication morphism $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to B[0]$ is an isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], then the standard cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] is zero in $D(B)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-flat-base-change] with C=B, A′=B, and C′=B. Writing f:A→B for the given homomorphism, the four maps in the square are A→C=f, A→A′=f, C→C′=id_B, and A′→C′=id_B. Thus the square commutes, and its canonical derived multiplication morphism is exactly the assumed isomorphism B⊗_A^{\mathbf L}B→B[0]. The cited base-change statement gives an isomorphism L_{B/A}⊗_B^{\mathbf L}B≃L_{B/B} in D(B). Derived extension of scalars along id_B is the identity (the ordinary functor -⊗_B B is naturally the exact identity functor), so L_{B/A}≃L_{B/B}.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-localization-cotangent-vanishing] with R=B and S={1}. This is a multiplicative subset, S^{-1}B is canonically B, and the node states that L_{S^{-1}B/B} is zero. Hence L_{B/B}=0. Transporting this zero object across the isomorphism from Step 1 proves that L_{B/A} is zero in D(B).
